commits.subject: phase 2 S7: the signature record, its retention and its two routes
phase 2 S7: record tests separate each lifelong kind and read long lines back

report.summary:
I built slice S7, the signature record of spec 6.8, on branch p2-s7 in worktree <scratch>/wt/p2-s7. The work is two commits on top of 587e18e, and the whole check list passed on the head, 3e88e58.

Only the two slice files changed: node/record.go (+336/-9) and node/record_test.go (+551). I did not touch node.go, the Node struct, commit or the route registration.

What the node does now:
- **Rolling record.** After each commit it appends one rolling entry (RecordEntry) to the segment file <snapshot>.record/<first height, 20 digits>.jsonl. A segment covers 10,000 heights from its first one and is named after that height, so gaps left by catch-up are handled.
  - Each entry holds Height, PreviousBlockHash, SealedDigest (ledger.SealedDigestOf over the nonce, the state digest and the content hash), the proposal of the deciding round, the commit, and KeepUntilHeight.
  - KeepUntilHeight is h + the pre-block RetainBlocks, and never less than the entry before it in the same segment.
  - The signing set is written in the first entry of a segment, and wherever its ValidatorsHash differs from the entry before's. Otherwise the field is empty.
- **No record state in memory.** The node reads the last complete line of the newest segment back from disk at each commit. To decide whether the set changed, it recomputes that entry's block hash with the new set's ValidatorsHash and compares it with the entry's Commit.BlockHash: the two are equal only if the set is the same.
- **Lifelong record.** For a block with a parameter change, a ⅔ name action (Reassignment), vote evidence or proposal evidence, it appends a LifelongRecordEntry to <snapshot>.lifelong.jsonl. The Signers field lists each name that signed something in the entry, once, in name order. The key is the name's account key before the block (the key its signature was checked under); the power is its power in the signing set, 0 for a name that is not a validator.
- **Pruning.** At each commit it deletes the oldest whole segments once the new height is past both their last KeepUntilHeight and their last height plus the current RetainBlocks.
- **Partial lines.** A partial last line, left by a write that failed, is skipped when read and replaced by the next write. This also works when lines are longer than the 64 KiB read back first.
- **Failures.** A failed write is logged and never stops the node. A node with no SnapshotPath records nothing.
- **Routes.** GET /hdls/record and /hdls/lifelong-record take ?from=H&count=N and return a JSON array of the entries with height ≥ H, at most N, and never more than 100. They start reading at the segment that holds H, skip partial lines and segments deleted meanwhile, and answer `[]` when there is no record.

How I read NameRequests: they are holder requests (registration, key change, bank change and freeze). Spec 6.8 says "holder requests ... are never written", and its LifelongRecordEntry has no field for them. So a block whose only governance-like content is name requests, freezes included, has no lifelong entry. Only the ⅔ name action counts as governance. The test pins this with a block that carries a freeze and a key change.

Proof the tests work: in a scratch copy I applied 29 mutants to record.go, each run with -count=3, and all 29 were caught (log: <scratch>/p2-scratch/s7/mutants-final.txt; the script that applies them is mutate.py beside it). The first mutant is the parent's stub bodies, emulated because the test file cannot compile against the parent, whose record.go has no RecordEntry type. All ten tests fail against it.

tests.name: TestRecordKeepsCertificatesAndNeverPayments
tests.failsWithoutChange: Fails with the stub bodies: no entries. Fails with a mutant that adds the block to the entry, and with one that writes the payers' names: the payment signature, or the JSON string "alice", is then found in the record.

tests.name: TestRecordNeverHoldsTheBareStateDigest
tests.failsWithoutChange: Fails with the stubs. Fails with SealedDigest replaced by block.StateDigest, and with the block added to the entry. It searches every record file for each committed block's state digest and nonce, as JSON, hex, base64 and raw bytes.

tests.name: TestRecordChainChecksFromItsOwnFields
tests.failsWithoutChange: Fails with the stubs, with the bare state digest, with the set written on every entry, and with the set left out of a segment's first entry. It recomputes each block hash with the latest set the record holds and checks it against the commit and the proposal. It then verifies both signatures, follows PreviousBlockHash back to the genesis hash, and matches the last entry to the node's last block hash.

tests.name: TestRecordPrunesWholeSegmentsAfterKeepUntilHeight
tests.failsWithoutChange: Fails with the stubs, with no pruning, with pruning at height <= instead of <, with an inclusive segment boundary (h <= first+10000), and with the set left out of the second segment's first entry.

tests.name: TestRetentionCutAppliesOnlyToNewRecords
tests.failsWithoutChange: Fails with the stubs. Fails when KeepUntilHeight is not kept at least the entry before's, when it uses the current RetainBlocks instead of the pre-block value, and when pruning ignores KeepUntilHeight. Also fails with no pruning, pruning at <=, and the inclusive boundary.

tests.name: TestLongerRetentionKeepsOldSegments
tests.failsWithoutChange: Fails with the stubs, and when pruning ignores 'last height + current RetainBlocks'. Also fails with no pruning, pruning at <=, and the inclusive boundary.

tests.name: TestLifelongRecordKeepsGovernanceAndEvidence
tests.failsWithoutChange: Fails with the stubs, and when name requests are made lifelong. Fails when any one of the four lifelong kinds (parameter change, name action, vote evidence, proposal evidence) is dropped from the rule. Fails when a signer's key is taken from the set (the outsider's key is then empty), when Signers are unsorted, or when evidence names are left out of Signers. Also fails with no from-filter on the route and with a zero BlockHash.

tests.name: TestRecordRoutesServeAtMostAHundredEntries
tests.failsWithoutChange: Fails with the stubs (empty body), with no 100 cap, with no from-filter, when a query missing from/count or with count < 0 is accepted, and when parameter changes are not lifelong.

tests.name: TestPartialLastLineIsSkipped
tests.failsWithoutChange: Fails with the stubs, when the reader serves a valid-JSON partial line, and when the writer appends after the partial line instead of replacing it. Also fails when the tail read never reads past its first 64 KiB, or does not check that the line starts inside the part read. Plus the set-always and bare-state-digest mutants.

tests.name: TestNodeWithoutASnapshotPathRecordsNothing
tests.failsWithoutChange: Fails with the stubs (the routes answer an empty body, not []), and when the SnapshotPath guard is removed: files then appear in the working directory. Extra test, not in the spec's list.

report.deviations:
None of these touches a file outside the slice. They are readings where the spec is open:
1. **No in-memory state.** The record keeps nothing in memory. Each commit reads the last line of the newest segment, and of the oldest segment for pruning. It tells a set change by recomputing the block hash of the entry before with the new set's ValidatorsHash. This avoids a new Node field in node.go.
2. **Pruning.** The spec says "deletes the oldest segment once...". The code deletes oldest segments in a loop while each one qualifies, so several can go at one commit (after a long gap). If a segment's last line does not parse, pruning stops and logs an error, rather than delete records that may still be within retention.
3. **Route queries.** Both from and count are required; otherwise, or for count < 0, the route answers 400. A count above 100 is cut to 100, not refused. The entries are served as written (json.RawMessage), not decoded and encoded again.
4. **Signers.** Each signer's key comes from the pre-block state's account, which for a validator is also the set's key. Power comes from the signing set. Names are listed once, in name order. The name action's NewKeySignature is not counted as a name's signature: the key that made it is the action's NewKey, which the entry already holds.
5. **File permissions.** Record files are 0o600 and the directory is 0o700, like the snapshot. Record writes are not fsynced: the record is best-effort, and a partial line left by a crash is replaced by the next write.
6. **Extra test.** I added TestNodeWithoutASnapshotPathRecordsNothing, beyond the spec's list, for the SnapshotPath guard.
report.suite:
All checks passed on 3e88e58 (log: <scratch>/p2-scratch/s7/suite-1.log), with GOTOOLCHAIN=auto, go1.27.3:
- `gofmt -l .` printed nothing outside review/.
- `go vet ./...` and `go vet -C ui ./...` passed.
- `go build ./...` and `go build -C ui -o /dev/null .` passed.
- `GOLEDGER_CHAOS_SLACK=4 go test -race -count=1 ./...` passed twice: consensus 55.8 s / 56.7 s, ledger 13.5 s / 13.0 s, node 62.2 s / 61.5 s, and cmd/demo, cmd/server and signing.
- The same with `-C ui` passed twice: 30.1 s / 30.2 s.
- `GOLEDGER_CHAOS_SLACK=4 go test -race -count=3 -run 'Chaos|Restart|SignLog|Resume|CatchUp' ./node/` passed in 93.0 s.

The ten record tests take about 0.8 s together (about 3 s each under -race -count=3). No time limit was raised.
report.openIssues:
1. **One unexplained failure.** During the first mutant pass, TestRecordKeepsCertificatesAndNeverPayments failed once under a mutant that does not touch it, and the failure text was not kept. It did not come back in 4 repeats, in 90 runs under -race, or in 450 runs under parallel load.
   - The one cause I found: the test searched for the bare text `alice`, and the record is mostly random base64, which spells that by chance about once in 10^4 runs. It now searches for the quoted JSON strings `"alice"` and `"Payments"`, which base64 cannot contain.
   - I cannot rule out another, timing-related cause.
2. **Route cost.** A route request scans the segment that holds `from` from its start and decodes each line's height. With 4 validators that is up to about 180 MB per request, and anyone can call the route (rate limits are a non-goal in the spec).
   - Picking the starting segment is only an optimisation: it has no test that fails without it, because reading every segment gives the same answer.
3. **A height can be recorded twice.** If the snapshot write fails but the record write succeeds, and the node then restarts from the older snapshot, it records that height again.
4. **Old record files are not detected.** At a new genesis, an operator who deletes the snapshot and sign log but keeps <snapshot>.record and <snapshot>.lifelong.jsonl gets the new network appended to the old files. Spec 0.2 covers only the snapshot and the sign log. The owner may want Open to refuse such files, or the record to carry the network id. The docs (S11) should at least tell operators to remove them.
5. **The record writes nothing until S10 lands.** Until then the chain never idles, so a busy test or demo network records every block. Under S10, an idle chain records nothing.
6. **S6 should check its evidence.** S6 may change how evidence is checked (the current-key rule). The Signers keys come from the pre-block accounts, which matches that rule. S6 should confirm that its evidence is still checked under the pre-block account key, or the lifelong Signers would name the wrong key.

problems.problem: No test fails when pruning uses the pre-block RetainBlocks instead of the current (post-block) value. Spec 6.8 says deletion waits for 'its last height plus the current RetainBlocks', so a longer retention applies at once. The production code is right (it uses node.state after commit replaced it), but the boundary at the block that raises the retention is not pinned.
problems.evidence: Mutant 'prune-uses-pre-block-retention': in recordCommittedBlock, node.state.Parameters.RetainBlocks is set to previousState's value around the pruneRecord call. It SURVIVED all ten record tests (log: <scratch>/p2-scratch/verify-S7-logs/mutants.txt). My test TestVerifyRaiseAppliesAtItsOwnBlock commits 1, 10000 and 10001 at retention 1000, then commits 11001 with retention 5000. It passes on HEAD and fails under the mutant: 'segments [00000000000000010001.jsonl] at the raise, want both'.
problems.fix: In TestLongerRetentionKeepsOldSegments, raise the retention at the height where the old value would prune: record.commit(1, 10000, 10001), then record.commitBlock(11001, ledger.BlockContent{}, 5000), and require both segments to remain.

problems.problem: No test covers a record file whose only content is a partial line, which is left when the first write of a new segment, or of the lifelong file, fails partway. lastCompleteLine handles it by returning offset 0, so the next write replaces the partial line. Without that, the next entry is glued onto the partial line and lost to readers. TestPartialLastLineIsSkipped only cuts lines short after complete lines.
problems.evidence: Mutant 'lone-partial-kept' changes `return nil, 0, nil` to `return nil, size, nil` in the no-newline branch. It SURVIVED all ten tests. My test TestVerifyLonePartialLineReplaced seeds the segment file and the lifelong file with only `{"Height":1,"Prev` and then commits height 1. It passes on HEAD and fails under the mutant: '/hdls/record served [] after a lone partial line'.
problems.fix: In TestPartialLastLineIsSkipped (or a few lines beside it), write a partial line as the whole content of a fresh segment file and of the lifelong file before their first entry. Then check that the next commit is served and that each file holds whole lines.

problems.problem: A height can be recorded twice, and the duplicate breaks the spec 6.8 check that each entry's PreviousBlockHash is the hash of the entry before. This is the builder's open issue 3, and I confirmed it. It happens when saveSnapshot fails but the record write succeeds, and the node restarts from the older snapshot and decides that height again from the re-gossiped last proposal and commit. A snapshot is a large atomic write, so it is more likely to hit ENOSPC than an 18 KB append.
problems.evidence: TestVerifyHeightRecordedTwice (in the scratch copy verify-S7-2) commits 1, 2 and 3, sets state.Height back to 2 and commits 3 again. The record holds heights [1 2 3 3].
problems.fix: One guard in writeRecordEntry, after `before` is decoded: return nil when before.Height >= block.Height. It needs the same Height check for the lifelong file (or the lifelong write skipped when the rolling write was skipped). Otherwise the owner accepts it and S11 documents it.

problems.problem: Route cost: readEntries reads the segment that holds `from` from its start and runs json.Unmarshal over every full line to learn its Height. The route is unauthenticated, so any client can make a validator scan up to a whole segment per request (builder open issue 2). Rate limits are a spec non-goal, so this is for the owner to weigh, not a spec violation.
problems.evidence: TestVerifyRouteCost builds a 35 MB segment of 2,000 entries of about 18 KB and asks /hdls/record?from=2000&count=1. It took 260 ms with a warm cache. Scaled to a full segment of 10,000 entries, that is about 1.3 s per request with 4 validators (184 MB) and about 5 s with 21 (720 MB), and requests can run in parallel.
problems.fix: Optional, about 5 lines: every line starts with `{"Height":`, so read the height from that prefix with strconv.ParseInt instead of decoding the whole line. Otherwise state the cost in docs/security.md (S11).

problems.problem: Record files left from an earlier network are not detected (builder open issue 4). At a new genesis with the same SnapshotPath, the new chain's entries are appended to the old network's newest segment. The route then serves old and new heights mixed together, and pruning stalls until the new chain passes the old heights. Spec 0.2 only covers the snapshot and the sign log, and the fix lies outside S7's files.
problems.evidence: TestVerifyStaleRecordAtNewGenesis: one node records 50000 and 50001, then a fresh node at the same SnapshotPath records 1 and 2. Result: segments [00000000000000050000.jsonl], and /hdls/record?from=0 serves [50000 50001 1 2].
problems.fix: S11 tells operators to delete <snapshot>.record/ and <snapshot>.lifelong.jsonl together with the snapshot and sign log at a new genesis. A code check would belong to a later slice that owns Open.

verdict.evidence:
I checked worktree p2-s7 at 3e88e58 (two commits on 587e18e; only node/record.go and node/record_test.go changed) against spec §0, §6.8, §6.10, §9.3, §10.2 S7, §12 and the Review record. I did not modify the worktree; all experiments ran in scratch copies verify-S7-1 and verify-S7-2 under <scratch>/p2-scratch/, with logs in verify-S7-logs/ and tools in verify-S7-tools/.

Scope (§10.2, §6.8):
- RecordEntry and LifelongRecordEntry match the spec structs, with Go field names and no tags.
- Rolling segments are <snapshot>.record/<20-digit first height>.jsonl, 10,000 heights each. The set is written in a segment's first entry and wherever ValidatorsHash changes. The change is detected by recomputing the previous entry's block hash with the new set, which is equivalent to comparing the two hashes.
- SealedDigest is SealedDigestOf(nonce, stateDigest, contentHash), the same as ledger/hash.go.
- KeepUntilHeight is h plus the pre-block RetainBlocks, never less than the previous entry in the same segment.
- Pruning deletes whole oldest segments once height is past both the last entry's KeepUntilHeight and its last height plus the post-block RetainBlocks.
- The lifelong entry is written for ParameterChange, Reassignment (the ⅔ name action), VoteEvidence and ProposalEvidence. Reading NameRequests (freezes included) as holder requests that are never written is consistent with §6.8 ('holder requests ... are never written') and §1's non-goal 'any history of holder requests'.
- Signers: names deduplicated and sorted. The key is the pre-block account key. That matches evidenceError (current account key) and SetFor, which takes set keys from the accounts. Power comes from the signing set, 0 for a non-validator.
- Routes: from and count are required, count is capped at 100, partial lines are skipped, and the answer is [] with no record.
- Nothing is recorded without SnapshotPath, and failed writes are only logged.
- Nothing from a later slice is built, and there are no old-format paths. The builder's six deviations are reasonable readings.

Adversarial tests (scratch verify-S7-2/node/record_verify_test.go, run with -race), all passing on HEAD:
- A 4-validator restartNetwork with one validator powered off and restarted: every node's record passes the full §6.8 check (block hash recomputed with the record's set, Commit.Verify, Proposal.Verify, PreviousBlockHash chain, heights increasing). The restarted node shows a catch-up gap (9 of 14 entries).
- Routes read concurrently with 300 commits of 40 KB entries: 62 reads, every one a JSON array of whole, consecutive entries.
- lastCompleteLine compared with a naive reading over 405 combinations of line sizes around the 64 KiB and 128 KiB boundaries.
- A set that changes and changes back is written each time.
- A jump far ahead prunes every old segment at once and starts a new one with its set.

Mutants (my own, independent of the builder's; log verify-S7-logs/mutants.txt):
- Stub bodies, kept with the types because the test file needs them: all ten tests fail.
- Killed: sealed digest without the nonce, inverted set test, power 0, count off by one, from exclusive, lifelong file truncated, KeepUntilHeight from the wrong segment, proposal dropped, commit dropped, zero previous hash, segment size 9999, cap 200, each kind of signer skipped, route starting at the newest segment.
- Survived, now listed as minor problems: pruning with the pre-block retention, and a lone partial line kept.
- Survived, and is only an optimisation: route-start-exclusive.

Flake check: 240 runs of the ten record tests under -race, 6 processes in parallel, all passed. The builder's one unexplained failure did not recur.

Full suite on HEAD (log verify-S7-logs/suite.log and ui.log), all with GOTOOLCHAIN=auto and go1.27.3:
- gofmt -l printed nothing.
- go vet for root and ui passed.
- go build for root and `go build -C ui -o /dev/null .` passed.
- GOLEDGER_CHAOS_SLACK=4 go test -race -count=1 ./... passed twice: consensus 54.4 s / 59.8 s, ledger 11.9 s / 13.2 s, node 62.1 s / 61.4 s, plus cmd/demo, cmd/server and signing.
- The ui run passed twice, 30.6 s / 30.0 s. My first ui invocation put -C after other flags and was rejected, so I reran it correctly.
- GOLEDGER_CHAOS_SLACK=4 go test -race -count=3 -run 'Chaos|Restart|SignLog|Resume|CatchUp' ./node/ passed in 93.9 s.

Naming, comments and commits: names are spelled out, receivers are named after their types (node, server, record), and error names follow the existing closeErr pattern. I found no dead code and the comments are accurate. Commit messages follow the 'phase 2 S7:' format with the trailer. Code is 288 non-comment lines (spec estimate about 210) and tests 473 (estimate about 270); the extra comes from the partial-line handling and from keeping no state in memory, which is justified because node.go is outside the slice.

fixed: Problem 1 (minor, test): no test pinned that pruning uses the current RetainBlocks. Commit 9596b64 'phase 2 S7: a longer retention applies from the block that carries it (review follow-up)' changes TestLongerRetentionKeepsOldSegments in node/record_test.go. It now commits 1, 10000 and 10001, raises the retention to 5000 at 11001 (the first height at which the old retention of 1000 deletes the first segment), then commits 15000, keeps both segments, and at 15001 keeps only the second. Proof: under the check's mutant prune-uses-pre-block-retention, the test as it was at 3e88e58 passes, and the new test fails with 'segments [00000000000000010001.jsonl] at height 15000, want both'. Log: <scratch>/p2-scratch/s7-followup/mutant-1.txt.

Problem 2 (minor, test): no test covered a file whose only content is a cut line. Commit ac0d01f 'phase 2 S7: a file that holds only a cut line is written over (review follow-up)' changes TestPartialLastLineIsSkipped. It now first writes a cut line as the whole content of the first segment file and of the lifelong file. It checks that the routes serve nothing, then that after heights 1 to 3 they serve 1 to 3 and each file holds only whole lines. The cutShort helper now creates a missing file. Proof: under the check's mutant lone-partial-kept, the test as it was at 3e88e58 passes, and the new test fails with '/hdls/record served heights [2 3], want 1 to 3'. Log: <scratch>/p2-scratch/s7-followup/mutant-2.txt.

Problem 3 (minor, code): a height could be recorded twice, and the duplicate broke the spec 6.8 PreviousBlockHash check. Commit eb7ca7d 'phase 2 S7: each height is recorded once (review follow-up)' adds one 8-line function to node/record.go, placeOfNextLine(path, height). It is lastCompleteLine plus one check: it refuses a height at or below the height of the file's last complete line. The error names the file and is logged like every other record failure. Both writes now call it, the rolling one in writeRecordEntry and the lifelong one in recordCommittedBlock. The file's header comment now says each height is recorded once. The new test TestRecordHoldsEachHeightOnce commits 1 to 4 (with parameter changes at 3 and 4), goes back to the hash of block 2, commits 3 and 4 again, then commits 5. It requires /hdls/record to serve [1 2 3 4 5] and /hdls/lifelong-record to serve [3 4]. Proof: with the record.go of ac0d01f (the parent commit) it fails with '/hdls/record served heights [1 2 3 4 3 4 5], want [1 2 3 4 5]'. It also fails when only the rolling file is checked, when only the lifelong file is checked, with > instead of >=, and with == instead of >=. Log: <scratch>/p2-scratch/s7-followup/mutant-3.txt (the mutation script is mutate.sh beside it).
No file outside the slice was touched: the three commits change only node/record.go and node/record_test.go.
notFixed: Problem 4 (minor, route cost): not changed, left for the owner to weigh. Rate limits are a non-goal in the spec, and the check marks the change optional. I measured the suggested change on the check's 35 MB segment (2,000 entries of about 18 KB) with a warm cache. The route as built takes about 255 ms. Reading the height from the line's prefix still takes about 97 ms, because bufio copying each 18 KB line costs more than decoding it (log: <scratch>/p2-scratch/s7-followup/route-cost.txt). So the change saves about 2.6 times, and a request still reads a whole segment. The parse would also depend on Height being the first JSON field. The served lines would then need a json.Valid check, because writeJSON encodes json.RawMessage and drops the whole response if one line is invalid. Making the cost smaller than a whole segment needs an index or rate limits, which is more than this slice. S11 should state the cost in docs/security.md.

Problem 5 (minor, record files left from an earlier network): not changed. A check belongs in Open (node.go / persist.go), which is outside S7's files, and the check's own fix is documentation (S11): delete <snapshot>.record/ and <snapshot>.lifelong.jsonl along with the snapshot and the sign log at a new genesis. The new rule from problem 3 changes the symptom. Before, the new chain's entries were appended to the old file and the route served the two networks mixed: [50000 50001 1 2]. Now the newest old segment refuses every height at or below its last height. Each commit logs '<file> already reaches height 50001', and the route serves only the old entries. Once the new chain passes the old heights it appends again. I checked this with the check's scenario in a scratch test. The owner should know that the stale case now loses the new entries below the old heights, and logs that at every commit.
